definitions.explanation: Describing a person who predominantly uses their right hand for tasks like writing, eating, and throwing. Also used as a noun to mean a right-handed person.

examples.japanese: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{右利|みぎき}きです。
⟦{日本人|にほんじん}→日本人：10112_nihonjin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧90⟦パーセント→パーセント：01537_paasento⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{右利|みぎき}きだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that about 90 percent of Japanese people are right-handed.

examples.japanese: {右利|みぎき}き⟦{用|よう}→〜用：09842_you⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ハサミ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{左利|ひだりき}き→左利き：22396_hidarikiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{使|つか}い→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦づらい→〜づらい：18368_zurai⟧。
examples.english: Scissors designed for right-handed people are difficult for left-handed people to use.

notes:
USAGE:
Used both as a noun ({右利|みぎき}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧, a right-handed person) and as a descriptive noun ({右利|みぎき}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧, right-handed). In Japan, there has traditionally been pressure to use the right hand for eating with chopsticks, though this is less common in modern times.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {右利|みぎき}き⟦{用|よう}→〜用：09842_you⟧ (designed for right-handed use)
- {右利|みぎき}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (right-handed person)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{左利|ひだりき}き→左利き：22396_hidarikiki⟧: left-handed — the opposite
- {両利|りょうき}き: ambidextrous — able to use both hands equally
